name: Tikva
title: Father-in-law of the prophetess Huldah
summary: Tikva (also known as Tokhath in 2 Chronicles) was the father of Shallum, who was the husband of the prophetess Huldah. He was the son of Harhas. Tikva is primarily known through his family connection to the prophetess Huldah, who played a crucial role during King Josiah's religious reform.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Huldah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Tikva is mentioned as the father of Shallum, the husband of the prophetess Huldah, when King Josiah's envoys sought counsel from Huldah regarding the Book of the Law found in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In the parallel account in 2 Chronicles, Tikva (here called Tokhath) is mentioned as the father of Shallum in connection with the consultation with the prophetess Huldah.

keyEvents.title: Discovery of the Book of the Law in the temple
keyEvents.description: The reason Tikva's family became important was the discovery of the Book of the Law in the temple during King Josiah's reign, which led to an inquiry made to the prophetess Huldah through her husband Shallum, Tikva's son.

keyEvents.title: Huldah's prophecy concerning God's judgment
keyEvents.description: Through his daughter-in-law Huldah, who was married to his son Shallum, Tikvah's family became the channel for a decisive prophetic message about God's judgment on Judah due to idolatry.

keyEvents.title: Huldah's Prophecy of Josiah's Mercy
keyEvents.description: Huldah, who was connected to Tikvah's family, also conveyed God's promise that King Josiah would be spared from seeing the coming disaster because of his humble heart.
